source.title: Plug & Play Generative Networks: Conditional Iterative Generation of Images in Latent Space
source.authors: Anh Nguyen; Jeff Clune; Yoshua Bengio; Alexey Dosovitskiy; Jason Yosinski

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses latent-space activation maximization to visualize inputs for hidden neurons and reports what facets those neurons appear to detect. This is a different method from the claim’s cited examples, but it bears on whether image-model neurons have multiple facets or a shared job.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative results for two hidden neurons conditioned on their activations. It does not report numeric measurements of neuron polysemanticity. Results cited from prior work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a generative-model paper. Its hidden-neuron images are a qualitative demonstration of the PPGN method for Multifaceted Feature Visualization. It uses two hand-picked AlexNet conv5 neurons, already labelled face and text detectors, and frames the results as the method's capability. It never asks whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs, measures how common that is, or re-examines a neuron claimed to be polysemantic. No version's effect is measured, so the record's 'tests'/T2 and its V1/V6 links are not justified. The finding is related but distinct (facets of one detector) and is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but misplaced in emphasis. The authors mainly conclude that PPGNs, with a learned prior on the latent code, give higher-quality, more diverse, high-resolution samples for many condition networks (classes, captions). They name plug-and-play flexibility as the most useful property. Improved multifaceted feature visualization is a secondary demonstration, said to reveal diverse and sometimes unexpected facets of a neuron.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a learned generator prior and iterative sampling in latent feature space to visualize hidden-neuron facets; it is not a direct reproduction of the cited InceptionV1 example.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper states that generated diversity and quality vary with sampling settings, including noise and prior-step multipliers, but does not report those sweeps as measurements of the neurons’ polysemanticity.

fits_no_version.finding: PPGN sampling shows an AlexNet conv5 'face detector' neuron (196) is driven by several facets: human faces at different angles, dog faces, masks, and house windows resembling eye sockets. The authors call these unexpected facets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neurons in image classifiers are multifaceted: one detector responds to several distinct visual variants of its concept, including look-alike objects.

record.problems: The neuron results are qualitative, concern only two selected AlexNet neurons, and do not establish whether the facets are unrelated or how prevalent such neurons are. No uncertainty estimates are reported for these results.

untested.parts: No test of whether image-classifier neurons respond to unrelated inputs, and no prevalence estimate. Only two pre-selected monosemantic-labelled AlexNet neurons are visualized.
No study of initialization, regularization or noise as causes.
No comparison of architectures, activations or regularization.
No canonical polysemantic neuron is re-examined. The face neuron was never claimed polysemantic, and the rarity of unrelated mixtures is not assessed.
No comparison of activation ranges or explanation scoring.

record.verdict_notes: The record overstates relevance. Neurons were chosen as already-identified monosemantic detectors, and the diversity claim compares PPGN with earlier visualization methods, not neurons with any baseline. No verdicts are given because no row measures a version's effect.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test InceptionV1 neuron 4e:55 or quantify how common unrelated mixtures are across image-classifier neurons.
No transformer language models or language-neuron measurements.
Does not test superposition or whether feature capacity exceeds neuron count.
Does not test initialization, regularization, or training noise as causes of polysemanticity under sufficient capacity.
Does not compare activation functions, architectures, or regularization effects on the share of polysemantic neurons, or measure performance costs of reducing that share.
Visualizes one previously identified face-detector neuron; does not estimate how often canonical polysemantic neurons have a shared job or whether truly unrelated mixtures are rare.
Does not compare activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods.

rows.subject: AlexNet DNN trained on ImageNet; hidden neuron 196
rows.operation_detail: Generated images conditioned on the activation of hidden neuron 196 using PPGN sampling.

conditions.value: 196; previously identified as a face detector

rows.measure: Qualitative types of synthesized inputs that activate the neuron.
rows.value: The generated facets include human faces, dog faces, masks, and face-like house windows; the paper also describes objects that barely resemble faces.
rows.locator: Figure 6; Supplementary Figures S20 and associated text
rows.note: The examples show multiple input types, but most are faces or described as resembling faces. The study does not establish that the inputs are unrelated.
rows.check: This is a method demonstration on a neuron chosen because it is a known face detector. The facets shown (human faces, dog faces, masks, face-like windows) are variants of one detector. They are not presented or tested as unrelated inputs, and no canonical polysemantic neuron is re-examined. So the row bears on neither V1 nor V6, and no baseline or comparison exists.

rows.subject: AlexNet DNN trained on ImageNet; hidden neuron 243
rows.operation_detail: Generated images conditioned on the activation of hidden neuron 243 using PPGN sampling.

conditions.value: 243; previously identified as a text detector

rows.measure: Qualitative diversity of synthesized inputs that activate the neuron.
rows.value: The paper reports substantially improved diversity of samples and different facets for this neuron, without specifying the facet types in the text.
rows.locator: Supplementary Figure S19 and associated text
rows.note: The text reports diverse facets but does not describe them sufficiently to determine whether they are unrelated.
rows.check: This is a method demonstration on a known text-detector neuron. The text claims only improved sample diversity relative to previous visualization methods, which compares the study's own method with others. Facet content is not described, so it bears on no version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
